newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 7.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Monday.

- A senior Irish policeman from the state's new assets tracing squad flew to London on Sunday after the arrest of John Gilligan, the self-confessed prime suspect for the murder of journalist Veronica Guerin.
- Bertie Ahern, leader of the main opposition party Fianna Fail, did a major U-turn in virtually closing the door on a coalition with Labour after the next general election.

- The cost of public sector pensions is set to triple in real terms over the next 30 years in Ireland, swallowing up almost a third of total government pay, a senior Department of Finance official has revealed.
- Ireland will overtake Britain in the EU table of income per head by the year 2000, according to a parliamentary answer given to Scottish nationalist minister Alex Sammond.
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu expressed serious concern at perceptions in Europe that Israel is the main block to the momentum of the Middle East peace process.
- John Gilligan was being held at Heathrow Airport in London on Sunday after being arrested by British Customs officers under UK drug-trafficking legislation.
- Citibank, the biggest U.S. bank, is to receive grant aid of at least five million Irish pounds for its European administration headquarters which will be in Dublin.

- Fixed-rate mortgages are set to fall further by the end of the year if Ireland stays on track for Economic and Monetary Union, the chief operating officer of National Irish Bank, Philip Halpin said.
